# Sound It Out

> Sound It Out helps parents teach reading, math and grammar at home to children ages 4 to 8 (preschool, kindergarten, first grade and the start of second grade), and helps when a child is stuck in reading. Free tools show where to start and point to what may be causing the difficulty. 10-day plans teach one difficulty each, with printable pages, a short video for each day and sound tracks for the child ($19, one payment, 30-day money back). Single printable packs are free to download. Bundles cost $3 or $5.

## 10-day plans
- [Ears First](https://sounditoutreading.com/ears-first-10-day-listening-plan/): Cannot tell me the first sound of a word, or cannot rhyme. The goal: on day 10 your child hears the sounds in a short word. They say how it starts, push three sounds together into a word, and pull a word apart into its sounds.
- [Know Every Letter](https://sounditoutreading.com/know-every-letter-10-day-letter-recognition-plan/): Does not know many letters yet, or knows the big ones but not the small ones. The goal: on day 10 your child names all 26 letters, big and small, even in a typeface never seen in the book.
- [Eight Sounds That Stay](https://sounditoutreading.com/eight-sounds-that-stay-10-day-plan/): Does not know the letter sounds, or learns them and forgets them. The goal: on day 10 your child says the sound of eight letters, in any order, a day after the last lesson, and uses them to read short words never seen before.
- [From Sounds to Words](https://sounditoutreading.com/from-sounds-to-words-blending-plan/): Knows the sounds, but cannot put them together into a word. The goal: on day 10 your child reads words they have never seen before.
- [Look at Every Letter](https://sounditoutreading.com/look-at-every-letter-10-day-plan/): Guesses words from the first letter or the picture, or “reads” books from memory. The goal: on day 10 your child looks at every letter before saying a word, and reads words and sentences never seen before, with no picture to help.
- [Tell b from d](https://sounditoutreading.com/tell-b-from-d-10-day-plan/): Mixes up b and d. The goal: on day 10 your child tells b from d, in letters, in words never seen before, and in their own writing.
- [Words That Stick](https://sounditoutreading.com/words-that-stick-sight-words-10-day-plan/): Cannot remember common words like the, said and was. The goal: on day 10 your child reads 16 of the most common words, on their own and inside sentences never seen before.
- [Cap to Cape](https://sounditoutreading.com/cap-to-cape-silent-e-10-day-plan/): Reads short words like cat, but gets stuck on cake, rain and boat. The goal: on day 10 your child looks to the end of a word for a silent e, and reads words like cake, kite and hope never seen before.
- [Smooth Reading](https://sounditoutreading.com/smooth-reading-10-day-plan/): Reads slowly, one word at a time, or sounds out every word. The goal: on day 10 your child reads a short sentence they have never seen, smoothly, the way they would say it.
- [Read It, See It](https://sounditoutreading.com/read-it-see-it-10-day-plan/): Reads the words but cannot tell me what it said. The goal: on day 10 your child reads a short story they have never seen, tells you what happened, and draws it.
- [Hear It, Write It](https://sounditoutreading.com/hear-it-write-it-10-day-spelling-plan/): Can read simple words but cannot spell them. The goal: on day 10 your child writes short words they have never practiced, every sound in the right order, and reads each one back to check it.
- [Count It Up](https://sounditoutreading.com/count-it-up-10-day-math-plan/): Counts one thing twice, or cannot add two small groups yet. The goal: on day 10 your child counts a group by touching each thing once, knows which number is more, and adds two small groups within 10.
- [My First Sentences](https://sounditoutreading.com/my-first-sentences-10-day-sentence-writing-plan/): Can write some words, but not a sentence: no capital, no spaces, no period. The goal: on day 10 your child writes a sentence they have never written, with a capital, spaces and a period, and reads it back.
- [Start at the Top](https://sounditoutreading.com/start-at-the-top-10-day-handwriting-plan/): Letters are messy, start in the wrong place or face the wrong way. The goal: on day 10 your child starts every small letter in the right place, sits it on the line, and writes new words that you can read.

- [Talking, Vocabulary and Reading: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-vocabulary-and-talking/): research summary. The guide says the language of books usually has to be taught. The evidence is rated minimal. Every finding names its source.
- [Decodable Books for Beginners: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-decodable-books/): research summary. A good case for decodable books at the very start. Not forever. Every finding names its source.
- [Do Children Learn to Read Naturally? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-do-children-learn-to-read-naturally/): research summary. A major review says the idea that letters stand for sounds has to be taught to most children. Every finding names its source.
- [Dyslexia: Early Signs and What Helps, From Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-dyslexia-early-signs/): research summary. Two research reviews on the signs, the risk factors and the teaching that has support. Every finding names its source.
- [How Often Should a Child Practice Reading? Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-how-often-to-practice-reading/): research summary. Studies used short, regular sessions. A direct test of short against long was not found. Every finding names its source.
- [Does Rhyming Matter for Reading? What Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-does-rhyming-matter/): research summary. Rhyme is an easier first step. The teaching that helped reading most worked on single sounds. Every finding names its source.
- [Reading Longer Words: What the Research Guide Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-longer-words/): research summary. The guide gives a routine: find the parts you know, say them, say them fast, check. Every finding names its source.
- [An Older Child Still Learning to Read: The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-older-child-still-a-beginner/): research summary. Phonics still helped older struggling readers. So did reading aloud again and again. Every finding names its source.
- [Does Reading Tutoring Help? What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-tutoring/): research summary. Extra teaching in small groups has strong support for sounding out words. Every finding names its source.
- [Sound Games With or Without Letters? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-sound-games-with-letters/): research summary. Sound work done with letters had bigger effects on reading. Every finding names its source.
- [What Parents Can Do at Home: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-what-parents-can-do-at-home/): research summary. In a review of 14 studies, parents teaching specific skills had the largest effect. Every finding names its source.
- [Do Reading Apps Help Young Children? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-apps/): research summary. A positive average effect, with large differences from app to app. Every finding names its source.
- [Learning to Read in a Second Language: The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-english-as-a-second-language/): research summary. The guide reports English learners learning to read at the same rate in kindergarten to grade 2. Every finding names its source.
- [When to Worry About Reading: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-when-to-worry-about-reading/): research summary. The sources name risk signs and school screening. None gives an age to worry. Every finding names its source.
- [Does Being Read To Predict Reading? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-being-read-to-and-later-reading/): research summary. Shared reading helps language. Its effect on reading skills is less sure. Every finding names its source.
- [Early Signs of a Future Reader: What Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-early-predictors-of-reading/): research summary. Knowing letters and hearing the sounds in words are among six early skills with the strongest links. Every finding names its source.
- [Forgetting Letter Sounds: What the Research Guides Say](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-remembering-letter-sounds/): research summary. The guides do not explain the forgetting. They do set out what to do. Every finding names its source.

## Guides
- [Does Phonics Help With Speech Delay?](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-does-phonics-help-with-speech-delay/): Does phonics help with speech delay? How sounds in speech and sounds in reading connect, what to practice at home, and why to work with a speech therapist.
- [Handwriting Help for Kids With Dysgraphia](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-handwriting-help-for-kids-with-dysgraphia/): Handwriting help for kids with dysgraphia: what it is, simple supports at home, letter practice that helps, and tools like typing and talk-to-text.
- [How to Help a Child With ADHD With Reading at Home](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-help-a-child-with-adhd-with-reading/): How to help a child with ADHD with reading: short sessions, movement breaks, clear steps, one task at a time, and comprehension habits that keep focus.
- [How to Help a Child With Vowel Sounds](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-help-a-child-with-vowel-sounds/): How to help a child with vowel sounds: teach short vowels one at a time with pictures, practice e and i apart, then long vowels, silent e and vowel teams.
- [How to Help a Child Write Sentences](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-help-a-child-write-sentences/): How to help a child write sentences: say it first, count the words, write with spaces, then check for a capital and a period. Steps, games and examples.
- [How to Improve Reading Comprehension at Home](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-improve-reading-comprehension-at-home/): How to improve reading comprehension at home: talk about the story, ask questions before, during and after, retell it, and build new words every day.
- [How to Practice Spelling Words at Home](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-practice-spelling-words-at-home/): How to practice spelling words at home: say each sound, write a letter for it, check right away, and spread the week’s list over short daily sessions.
- [How to Teach a Child to Write Their Name](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-a-child-to-write-their-name/): How to teach a child to write their name: start each letter at the top, trace, copy, then write alone, with a capital first letter and small letters after.
- [How to Teach a Left-Handed Child to Write](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-a-left-handed-child-to-write/): How to teach a left-handed child to write: tilt the paper, hold the pencil a bit higher, sit on the left, and avoid smudges with simple, easy changes.
- [How to Teach Addition to Kindergarten](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-addition-to-kindergarten/): How to teach addition to kindergarten children at home: start with real objects, count all, then count on, and learn the facts within 5 and 10.
- [How to Teach Capital Letters and Periods](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-capital-letters-and-periods/): How to teach capital letters and periods: one rule at a time, a short checklist, and fixing sentences together, so your child writes them every time.
- [How to Teach Counting to Preschoolers](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-counting-to-preschoolers/): How to teach counting to preschoolers: say the numbers in order, touch one thing per number, and learn that the last number tells how many. With games.
- [How to Teach Phonics at Home: A Step-by-Step Guide](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-phonics-at-home/): How to teach phonics at home, step by step: listening first, letter sounds, blending short words, then letter teams, with a few minutes of practice a day.
- [How to Teach Reading to Kids With Autism at Home](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-reading-to-kids-with-autism/): How to teach reading to kids with autism at home: clear steps, visual supports, special interests, short routines and phonics in order, at their pace.
- [How to Teach Rhyming Words to Kids](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-rhyming-words/): How to teach rhyming words to kids at home: listening games, finding the odd one out, and making rhymes, with steps for preschool and kindergarten.
- [How to Teach Sight Words to a Kindergartener](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-sight-words-to-kindergarten/): How to teach sight words to a kindergartener at home: a few words a week, map each word to its sounds, and short daily games that make the words stick.
- [My 8 Year Old Doesn't Know How to Read: What to Do](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-my-8-year-old-doesnt-know-how-to-read/): My 8 year old doesn’t know how to read: why some children fall behind, how to find the missing skills, and how to teach reading step by step at home.

- [My Child Knows Sounds but Cannot Blend: What to Do](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-my-child-knows-sounds-but-cannot-blend/): What to do when your child knows the letter sounds but cannot blend them into words: why it happens, and simple blending steps to try this week.
